headline: Drupal's incomplete installer fix leaves sites open to takeover as attackers exploit Mitel, Juniper, and Palo Alto gear with AI help.

emerging_trends.text: National agencies in Italy and Switzerland and researchers at Accenture now describe autonomous agents driving intrusions, compressing reconnaissance and exploitation into minutes.

topics.title: Drupal Patch Gap Leaves Sites Exploitable
topics.latest_developments: Drupal disclosed CVE-2026-136716, a highly critical flaw already exploited in the wild, because its earlier Fail2Install fix left some sites in vulnerable installation states.
topics.why_it_matters: Site owners who applied the first patch and declared victory still face unauthenticated takeover across government, university, and media deployments.

details.label: What to do
details.text: Update Drupal core a second time. Hunt for unexpected site reinstalls, new administrator accounts, and changes to settings files.

details.label: Flashback
details.text: Attackers have exploited the original bug, CVE-2026-132165, since at least November 19, and CISA set a November 27 deadline for federal agencies.

sources.title: Drupal Warns of New Highly Critical Site Takeover Vulnerability Under Active Exploitation
Drupal Installer Patch Left a Gap Attackers Are Already Exploiting
Critical Drupal installer flaw under active attack (CVE-2026-132165)

topics.title: Attackers Exploit Mitel MiCollab Zero-Days
topics.latest_developments: Accenture said hackers exploited Mitel MiCollab flaws before Mitel published its advisory, likely with AI assistance, in a suspected extortion campaign.
topics.why_it_matters: MiCollab servers carry voice, chat, and directory data for entire organizations, and the attacks ran while no patch existed.

details.label: By the numbers
details.text: CISA added 10 flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Wednesday, among them five MiCollab bugs plus Juniper, Vates, and Danfoss products.

details.label: What to do
details.text: Patch MiCollab and audit the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing component for uploaded files under CVE-2026-133275. Pull management interfaces off the internet.

sources.title: Mitel MiCollab Zero-Days Exploited in Suspected AI-Assisted Attacks
Hackers Exploit 10 Vulnerabilities Across Mitel, Juniper, Vates, and Danfoss Products
CISA warns of critical unpatched flaw in Danfoss refrigeration controllers

topics.title: 1Password Says Attacker Copied Source Code
topics.latest_developments: 1Password said the attacker who hijacked an employee's corporate GitHub account copied source code from private repositories plus account records, and the investigation began November 19, 2026.
topics.why_it_matters: Stolen customer names and emails give phishers a vetted list of password manager users to impersonate 1Password against.

details.label: Zoom in
details.text: The attacker pushed malicious code into backend services before containment. 1Password says customer vaults and other secrets stayed inaccessible.

details.label: What to do
details.text: Verify any 1Password support contact through the company's own site, and review GitHub account protections for developers with production access.

sources.title: 1Password Hacked, Customer Data and Source Code Stolen in GitHub Account Breach
1Password breached through hijacked employee GitHub account, customer names and emails stolen
1Password Breach Exposes Customer Data, Internal Source Code

topics.title: Italy and Switzerland Flag Autonomous AI Attacks
topics.latest_developments: The Swiss and Italian national cyber agencies warned that attacks driven by autonomous AI agents are hitting critical infrastructure organizations in both countries.
topics.why_it_matters: Agent-driven attacks compress reconnaissance and exploitation into minutes, outrunning patch cycles and human-speed triage at utilities, transport, and manufacturing operators.

details.label: What to do
details.text: Unit 42 tells teams to baseline normal behavior and push detection to the edge, since agent-speed intrusions leave no room for manual review.

details.label: What to watch
details.text: Cyber insurers now sort clients into AI-defense haves and have-nots and say the current policy model cannot hold.

sources.title: Italy and Switzerland warn of autonomous AI-driven cyberattacks
The AI Threat Horizon: Why Speed, Edge AI and Baselines Are Our Best Defense
Cyber Insurers See New Divide: AI Defense 'Haves' & 'Have Nots'

topics.title: FIFA Confirms Hackers Accessed Personal Information
topics.latest_developments: FIFA, the Switzerland-based governing body for soccer, said a cyberattack reached a limited set of personal and business information, without naming a date or the data types.
topics.why_it_matters: FIFA holds records on players, officials, staff, and World Cup commercial partners, and the vague disclosure leaves affected people unable to judge their exposure.

details.label: What's next
details.text: FIFA says it is working with relevant authorities and law enforcement to investigate the breach.

sources.title: FIFA Says It Has Been Victim of a Cyberattack Accessing 'Personal and Business Information'
FIFA says hackers accessed 'limited set of personal and business information'

topics.title: SYS010 Malware Hijacks Browser Enterprise Management
topics.latest_developments: A new version of the SYS01 infostealer, SYS010, spreads through Meta ads and enrolls victim browsers into enterprise-style management to force-install a data-stealing extension.
topics.why_it_matters: The forced extension reads Gmail and Outlook mail, turning an ad click into persistent mailbox surveillance with no user consent prompt.

details.label: The big picture
details.text: A second stealer, Remus, pulls Gmail messages through a fake Google Sheets Chrome extension its operators marketed as a Gmail zero-day.

details.label: What to do
details.text: Alert on new browser cloud management policies and enrollment profiles appearing on endpoints, and block extension installs outside an approved list.

sources.title: SYS010 malware abuses browser management to spy on Gmail, Outlook
Remus malware steals Gmail messages via fake Google Sheets extension

topics.title: Fake Job Tests Hide Malicious NuGet Packages
topics.latest_developments: Socket researcher Kush Pandya found 13 malicious NuGet packages posing as WinUI 3 and Windows Presentation Foundation button controls inside fake take-home job assessments.
topics.why_it_matters: Building or running the sample project hands attackers access to a .NET developer's machine, and from there to source code and credentials.

details.label: What to do
details.text: Treat recruiter-supplied projects as untrusted code. Build them in disposable virtual machines and restrict developers to vetted package feeds.

sources.title: 13 Malicious NuGet Packages Turn Fake .NET Job Assessments Into Malware Delivery Traps
Attackers Target .NET Developers With Poisoned Job Assessments

topics.title: Prosecutors Indict Ransomware Recovery Co-Founder
topics.latest_developments: A federal grand jury in the District of Rhode Island indicted Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, 52, on three wire fraud counts for secretly paying ransoms.
topics.why_it_matters: Companies that hire recovery firms may be funding the gangs that attacked them, taking on sanctions and disclosure exposure they never approved.

details.label: Zoom in
details.text: Agents arrested Palacio Escobar, a Colombian national, in Las Vegas on October 22. Each count carries a maximum of 20 years in prison.

details.label: What to do
details.text: Require recovery vendors to state in writing whether they contact or pay attackers, and keep ransom decisions with the general counsel.

sources.title: Data recovery firm co-founder accused of cashing in on ransomware victims
Florida ransomware recovery CEO indicted for allegedly paying hacker ransoms

topics.title: North Korea's PolinRider Poisons GitHub Repositories
topics.latest_developments: SafeDep reported that the North Korea-linked PolinRider campaign planted a Python loader in more than 7,600 GitHub repositories, with evidence the activity started by February 2025.
topics.why_it_matters: Developers who clone and run a poisoned project hand attackers code execution on machines holding source code, cloud keys, and signing credentials.

details.label: Zoom in
details.text: The loader hides inside a small utils package or in conftest.py, so it fires the moment Python imports the file.

details.label: What to do
details.text: Scan repositories for unexpected conftest.py files and utils packages, and run untrusted projects only in disposable virtual machines.

sources.title: North Korea-Linked PolinRider Poisons Over 7,600 GitHub Repositories to Spread Malware

topics.title: Attackers Exploit Juniper Session Smart Conductor
topics.latest_developments: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-103406 in Juniper Session Smart Conductor to run arbitrary commands as root, and CISA added the flaw to its exploited catalog Wednesday.
topics.why_it_matters: Conductor sits at the center of Session Smart router deployments, so root command execution there exposes the network paths it manages.

details.label: What to do
details.text: Patch Session Smart Conductor now and keep its management interface off the public internet. Review Conductor hosts for unexpected root processes and new accounts.

sources.title: Critical Juniper Session Smart Conductor Flaw Exploited in Attacks
